note: Attacker-controlled '&' byte in JSX child text is reached when the parser buffer is exactly full (p == q == buffer + bufferSize - 1); the '&' is dispatched to entity parsing with p at the end of the allocated range.
Unchecked store of the leading '&' byte: no p < q bound check is performed for this first character, so the store executes at p == q and advances p one byte past the end of the allocated heap buffer.

The only bounds guard in the entity-name loop, (p < q), is now false because p was advanced past q by the unchecked '&' store; the loop is skipped and the out-of-range pointer is used by the following store.
Heap-buffer-overflow write: the null terminator is stored at p == buffer + bufferSize, one byte past the end of the allocated parser buffer (q + 1).
